mistakes.title: Forgetting the colon after if statement
mistakes.explanation: Beginners often forget to add a colon at the end of an if statement, thinking it's not necessary since they are used to other programming languages that may not require it.
mistakes.traceback:
File "<stdin>", line 2
    if score == 10
                  ^
SyntaxError: expected ':'
mistakes.fix: Always remember to add a colon ':' at the end of your if statements. Python will tell you there's a syntax error when it sees the missing colon.

mistakes.title: Incorrect indentation in the if block
mistakes.explanation: Beginners may not realize that Python uses indentation to define blocks of code, leading to confusion when they don't indent correctly.
mistakes.traceback:
File "<stdin>", line 3
    print("ten")
    ^^^^^
IndentationError: expected an indented block after 'if' statement on line 2
mistakes.fix: Make sure to indent the code inside the if block. Python raises an IndentationError when it expects an indented block but doesn't find one.

mistakes.title: Using a loop variable after the loop with an empty list
mistakes.explanation: Beginners might try to use a loop variable outside of the loop without realizing that the list was empty, leading to confusion about the variable's existence.
mistakes.broken_code:
my_list = []
for item in my_list:
    print(item)
print(item)
mistakes.traceback:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 4, in <module>
NameError: name 'item' is not defined. Did you mean: 'iter'?
mistakes.fix: Be aware that the loop variable is only defined within the loop. Python raises a NameError when you try to access it outside if the loop didn't run.
mistakes.fixed_code:
my_list = []
for item in my_list:
    print(item)
# The variable 'item' is not used here since the list is empty.
